HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Manga action frame with a hard 30-degree dutch tilt, medium-close at night in a muddy ditch. Yumjong (grey hair as on his sheet, a black rebel headband, his white robe with the crimson collar exactly as on his sheet portrait) thrusts a long WOODEN-SHAFTED SPEAR (a long pole with a small leaf-shaped iron head) and Yushin (bearded, dark blue robe), in the PLAIN blue robe from canon (no armour, no vest, no straps), holding his sword in ONE hand only with his other arm flung back for balance, beats the spear shaft aside: sparks burst where the straight blade bites the wooden shaft between their faces. Yumjong teeth bared; Yushin a fresh cut on his cheek, eyes cold. Mud flying, bold dry-brush sumi-ink speed lines along the spear and the blade, radial focus lines on the sparks, ink-splatter dirt. Torches on the wall above as orange bokeh. No lettering. ONE device: the X of wooden spear shaft and steel blade. FRAMING: the RIGHT frame edge cuts through Yushin's sword forearm, so his sword hand and the hilt are OUTSIDE the frame; only the long STRAIGHT blade enters from the right edge and meets the spear. Yushin's bearded face and shoulder are visible above his arm. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = yumjong, SECOND face = yushin. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_radiance_fortress (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), jougwan feather-cap board (shape only, ignore labels). BOTTOM ROW: the only sword design. YUMJONG Colour #8a68c9. KIM YUSHIN — Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Colour #2A5FB8. PLACE Radiance Fortress (명활성) — attached board /pl_radiance_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Myeonghwal (Radiance) Fortress: Bidam's mountain wall facing Wolseong across the field. Any sword is the ancient straight Korean ring-pommel dao: a small iron ring pommel, a short wrapped grip, a thin metal band and NO hand guard, a perfectly straight blade — never a katana, never a tsuba. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
